subject: biology
title: Treating kidney failure: dialysis and transplants
key_idea: (Separate science) When the kidneys fail, urea and excess ions build up in the blood. A dialysis machine removes them by diffusion, or a healthy donor kidney can be transplanted. Each treatment has advantages and disadvantages.

blocks.text: In kidney failure the kidneys can no longer remove enough urea from the blood. A dialysis machine does this job instead.

items.meaning: Cleaning the blood of a person with kidney failure by passing it through a machine.
The solution on the other side of the membrane. Unwanted substances diffuse into it.

diagram.alt: Dialysis in four steps: blood leaves the arm, passes the membrane in the machine, urea and excess ions diffuse into the dialysis fluid, and the cleaned blood returns to the body.
steps: Blood is taken from the arm into the dialysis machine
Blood and dialysis fluid are separated by a partially permeable membrane
Urea and excess ions diffuse into the dialysis fluid
Cleaned blood is returned to the body

items: Unwanted substances include urea and excess ions, such as sodium and chloride.
They diffuse across the membrane, down their concentration gradient, from the blood into the dialysis fluid.
Fresh dialysis fluid is pumped through to keep the concentration gradient steep.
The dialysis fluid has the same concentration of useful substances as healthy blood, so these are not lost from the blood.
A patient usually needs dialysis about three times a week. Each session lasts several hours and is often in hospital.
Urea and excess ions diffuse from the blood into the dialysis fluid.
A partially permeable membrane separates blood and dialysis fluid.
Fresh fluid keeps the concentration gradient steep.

blocks.text: A transplant replaces the failed kidney with a healthy kidney from a donor, in a surgical operation.

items: A person can live well with only one kidney, so a living donor can give one.
The donor kidney must be a tissue match, or the patient's immune system may attack it. This is **rejection**.
A twin has the same genes, so a kidney from a twin is less likely to be rejected.
The patient takes **immunosuppressant** drugs to reduce the chance of rejection.
A suitable donor kidney may not be available, so patients may have to wait.
A transplant needs a donor kidney with a tissue match.
Immunosuppressant drugs reduce the risk of rejection.
Donor kidneys are in short supply.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask you to weigh the two treatments. Use points for and against each, and reach a judgement.

rows: No regular visits, so more flexible
A working kidney keeps substances at the correct level
Skin is punctured repeatedly and blood meets a machine, so infection and blood clots are possible
One operation, with a risk from surgery and the anaesthetic
Immunosuppressants for the rest of life, which can lead to other infections
Needed for as long as the kidneys are failed
May be rejected or need replacing eventually

checks.q: Describe how dialysis removes urea from the blood.
checks.a: Blood passes through a machine, where it is separated from dialysis fluid by a partially permeable membrane. Urea diffuses across the membrane, down its concentration gradient, into the dialysis fluid.

checks.q: Why must a donor kidney be a tissue match?
checks.a: If it is not, the patient's immune system may attack it and the kidney is rejected.

checks.q: Give two disadvantages of a kidney transplant compared with dialysis.
checks.a: Any two from: the kidney may be rejected; immunosuppressant drugs must be taken; a suitable donor may not be available; risk from surgery; it may need replacing eventually.

worked_example.question: Some people have kidney failure. Doctors may treat patients with kidney failure by either dialysis or a kidney transplant. Explain two biological reasons why most doctors think that a kidney transplant is a better method of treatment than dialysis. Do not refer to cost or convenience.
answer_points: Reason 1: the concentrations of urea and other substances in the blood change less (or not at all) (1).
So there is less or no damage to body cells and tissues, for example they are not poisoned by urea (1).
Reason 2: the skin is not repeatedly punctured, or the blood does not leave the body or meet a machine (1).
So there is less chance of infection or blood clots, or no need to take anti-clotting drugs (1).
worked_example.tip: Each reason scores one mark and its explanation scores one more. The explanation must match the reason.

worked_example.question: Describe how dialysis removes unwanted substances from the blood. Include examples of unwanted substances in your answer.
answer_points: Dialysis is used when the kidneys are damaged and do not remove urea from the blood.
Blood is taken from the arm and passes into the dialysis machine.
The blood is separated from the dialysis solution by a partially permeable membrane.
Unwanted substances include urea and excess ions, such as sodium and chloride.
These move into the dialysis fluid by diffusion across the membrane, down a concentration gradient.
Fresh dialysis fluid is pumped through to maintain the concentration gradient, and the blood is returned to the body.
worked_example.tip: Cover the route of the blood, examples of unwanted substances and how they move. Keep the answer in a clear order.
